extra.extract: .NET My Services (codenamed Hailstorm) is an abandoned collection of XML-based Web services by Microsoft for storing and retrieving information. NET My Services was announced on March 19, 2001, as part of Microsoft's .NET initiative and was intended to rely on what was then known as a Microsoft Passport, a single sign-in web service now referred to as a Microsoft account. .NET My Services was a platform intended to facilitate the storage and retrieval of user-related information, such as contacts, calendar information, and e-mail messages, by allowing it to be accessed from a centralized repository across various applications and device types, including traditional desktop PCs, and mobile devices such as laptops, mobile phones, PDAs, and tablet PCs; access to this stored information would be based solely on user discretion. The technology would rely on a subscription-based business model. Although the technology required a Microsoft Passport, it was based on cross-platform, open standard web services, including SOAP, UDDI, and WS-Discovery, which enabled interoperability with compatible systems without requiring Microsoft Windows. After .NET My Services was announced on March 19, 2001, Microsoft intended for it to reach broad developer availability at that year's Professional Developers Conference, with a subsequent end-user release scheduled for 2002. However, due to industry concerns related to anti-competitive behavior and end-user privacy, the company ultimately abandoned the initiative before it could fully materialize.

{{image}}
=={{int:Taxonavigation}}==
{{Alsophis}}
Species: ''[[Alsophis antiguae]]''

=={{int:Name}}==
''Alsophis antiguae'' {{a|Hampton Wildman Parker|Parker}}, 1933

* {{int:Syntypes}}: {{rl|BMNH}} 1946.1.4.46-47 (formerly BMNH = 1850. 50.4.29.1–2), both juvenile ♀, collected by Gardiner, date unknown.
* {{int:Type locality}}: “Antigua”.

==={{int:Combinations}}===
* ''Alsophis leucomelas antiguae'' {{aut|Parker}}, 1933: 158 [original combination, as subspecies]
* ''Alsophis antiguae'' — {{aut|Parker}}, 1936: 228 [subsequent combination, elevated to species]
* ''Alsophis antillensis antiguae'' — {{aut|Schwartz}}, 1966: 216 [subsequent combination, reduced to subspecies]

==={{int:Synonyms}}===
* ''Alsophis antiguae sajdaki'' {{a|Robert William Henderson|Henderson}}, 1990: 119
** {{int:Holotype}}: [[KU]] 211059 (formerly ASPS V6789), ♀, collected by R. Thomas on 11 August 1965.
** {{int:Type locality}}: “Great Bird Island, St. George Parish, off of the northeastern coast of Antigua, Lesser Antilles”.

=={{int:Native distribution areas}}==
* Antigua and Barbuda: Barbuda (subfossil remains), Antigua (extinct) and Great Bird Island.

=={{int:References}}==
==={{int:Primary references}}===
* {{a|Hampton Wildman Parker|Parker, H.W.}} 1933. Some amphibians and reptiles from the Lesser Antilles. ''[[ISSN 0374-5481|Annals and Magazine of Natural History. Series 10]]'' 11(61): 151–158. {{doi|10.1080/00222933308673636}} {{Access|closed}}
* {{a|Robert William Henderson|Henderson, R.W.}} [1989] 1990. A new subspecies of ''Alsophis antiguae'' ({{aut|Parker}}) from Great Bird Island (Antigua), Lesser Antilles. ''[[ISSN 0008-6452|Caribbean Journal of Science]]'' 25(3–4): 119–122.
==={{int:Links}}===
* {{aut|Daltry, J. & Mayer, G.C.}} 2016. {{IUCN|CR|939}}. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2016: e.T939A71739009. {{doi|10.2305/IUCN.UK.2016-3.RLTS.T939A71739009.en}}. Accessed on 05 November 2023.

=={{int:Vernacular names}}==
{{VN |de=Antigua-Schlanknatter |en=Antiguan Racer}}

[[Category:Hampton Wildman Parker taxa]]
